question: For two years, from January 2024 onwards, Algeria will be a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council. This Islamic republic has been a member of the UN Human Rights Council, together with 46 other countries, since January 2023.

That is curious, given that the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights has voiced concern about ongoing discrimination against religious minorities and the systematic closure of non-Islamic places of worship. The UN Human Rights Council’s Universal Periodic Review of Algeria shows that the country is trifling with what is, after all, constitutionally enshrined freedom of religion.

The regime in Algeria does not shy away from outright persecution of religious minorities. Algeria nevertheless can boast an extensive partnership with the EU and is also an EU trading partner enjoying all the benefits of a free-trade area. 1.
What measures has the Commission taken during this parliamentary term with regard to the persecution of religious minorities and, in particular, Christians in Algeria?
Does the Commission anticipate taking measures, for instance within Euromed, while Algeria continues to discriminate against religious minorities?
Does the Commission anticipate suspending all aid and assistance to Algeria while religious minorities continue to be persecuted?
answer: Respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms is inscribed in the Algerian Constitution and constitutes a key element of EU-Algeria relations, as enshrined in the Association Agreement (1) and reinforced in the Partnership Priorities (2). Human rights and fundamental freedoms, including freedom of religion or belief, are addressed during the regular EU-Algeria political, security and human rights dialogue.

The EU does not currently envisage the suspension of ongoing cooperation with Algeria. Instead, the EU favours frank and constructive discussions and is committed to support the implementation of political reforms envisaged by the Algerian authorities to enhance the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms, including freedom of religion or belief.

Euro-Mediterranean Agreement establishing an Association between the European Community and its Member States, of the one part, and the People’s Democratic Republic of Algeria, of the other part, OJ n° L 265, 10 October 2005. Shared Partnership Priorities of the People's Democratic Republic of Algeria and the European Union under the revised European Neighbourhood Policy (ENP), UE-AL 3101/17 ADD 1, Brussels 7 March 2017.
